Subject: Request: Erasure & data transfer — patient record (GDPR)

Hi Evelyn,

I’m Julia Smith, DPO at ACME Health. We are submitting a formal GDPR erasure request for patient identifier ACME-PAT-8821 and any associated PII stored by Redwood Inference related to our account. Please confirm the scope of data you hold (including backups and analytics exports) and provide a timeline for complete deletion, plus a signed statement confirming whether Redwood acted as controller or processor for any transfers of that data (particularly any transfers to third parties such as analytics vendors).

For identity verification, I’ve attached a redacted company letter (identity_proof_julia.pdf) and we can provide a DSAR form if needed. Our expectation under the contract is deletion within 30 days, and we need an evidence bundle showing deletion and proof of notification to downstream processors (if applicable).

Please advise next steps and a contact for evidence delivery (we prefer encrypted SFTP or a signed PDF bundle).

Thanks,
Julia Smith
DPO, ACME Health
j.smith@acmehealth.com

Subject: Internal: ACME erasure scope & ops plan

Team,

Summary: ACME (ACME-PAT-8821) submitted an erasure + transfer confirmation request. They’re in EU jurisdiction; they want deletion evidence and confirmation re: transfers to third parties (specifically asked about analytics vendors).

Proposed immediate steps:
1) Identity & scope: Confirm account IDs with Julia (Evelyn to send CP statement).
2) Data mapping: Run query across hosted buckets + embeddings index + S3 exports for ACME account within the last 5 years. (SRE: PRIV-742 SLA 48h scope run).
3) Backups: Check snapshot retention windows and identify any snapshots containing the PID. Need backup owner (storage team) to schedule targeted snapshot pruning where feasible; otherwise document retention exception and flagged deletion when snapshot rotation completes.
4) Downstream processors: Query transfer logs (routing service) for any outbound flows to vendors (Medlytics?). If transfers occurred, compile notification list and prepare processor-notification letters.
5) Evidence bundle: Use erasure_playbook_v2.docx as template + SCCs_mapping.xlsx for legal.
6) Communications: We should provide a controller/processor statement before executing deletion. Vivek, can you confirm the standard wording?

I’ll kick off the mapping queries and attach the preliminary manifests to PRIV-742.

Attachments: erasure_playbook_v2.docx; SCCs_mapping.xlsx

Karthik
Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference

Hi Julia / Evelyn,

Quick update and clarifying positions: 
- Controller/Processor: For the standard Redwood inference hosting we are a processor acting on ACME’s instructions. If ACME has independently arranged data export flows (server-to-server) that we configured but did not control, we may be acting as a processor facilitating the transfer; each transfer will be listed in the manifest. 
- Medlytics: We see a single scheduled export job to medlytics-analytics-prod that matches ACME-Prod-4781 activity. We will notify Medlytics and request confirmation of deletion. If Medlytics is a subprocessor under Redwood (per contract), Redwood will obtain their deletion statement; if they are engaged directly by ACME, we will provide logs showing the transfer and assist ACME in obtaining deletion confirmation.

Operational actions (already in progress):
1) SRE: running mapping query and producing a scoped manifest (expected EOD today).
2) Backup check: storage team to flag involved snapshots for expedited retention review; where immediate deletion of snapshot data is not possible we will document retention exceptions and expected removal date.
3) Notifications: Legal will issue the processor notification template to Medlytics and request a signed deletion receipt.
4) Evidence bundle: We will deliver an encrypted S3 link with a PGP-signed manifest containing: file-level delete stamps, transfer logs (redacted as necessary), and copy of processor notification letters.

I will follow up with the PGP key and the S3 link once the bundle is ready. Expected end-to-end: 10-30 days depending on third-party responsiveness and snapshot retention.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Legal & Compliance, Redwood Inference
